You don’t want to think about what, exactly, the network is doing every time you open a browser and go to http://google.com, and, these days, you don’t have to. In fact, I would argue that it’s fantastic that computer interfaces have advanced to the point where most people who use the internet

get information to your browser, let’s use the following example. Alice owns a web server. Bob uses a desktop computer, which is trying to connect to Alice’s server. When one machine wants to talk to another machine, something like the following exchange takes place: 1. Bob’s computer sends along a stream of 1 and 0 bits, indicated by high and low voltages on a wire. These bits form some information, containing a header and body. The header contains an immediate destination of his local router’s MAC address, with a final destination of Alice’s IP address. The body contains his request for Alice’s server application. 2. Bob’s local router receives all these 1s and 0s and interprets them as a

IP address. 5. Alice’s server reads the packet port destination in the header, and passes it off to the appropriate application—the web server application. (The packet port destination is almost always port 80 for web applications; this can be thought of as an apartment number for packet data, whereas the IP address is like the street address.) 6. The web server application receives a stream of data from the server processor. This data says something like the following: - This is a GET request. - The following file is requested: index.html. 7. The web server locates the correct HTML file, bundles it up into a new packet to send to Bob, and sends it through to its local router, for transport

packets of information, telling your operating system to send them off, and interpreting the data you get back as pretty pictures, sounds, videos, and text. You need to evaluate batches of outputs not individual ones. And you need something that runs continuously because the quality can drift over time without you changing a single line of code. In this article, I'll walk you through building a complete evaluation pipeline. We'll also cover three different evaluation strategies that work at different levels of cost and depth. Grab the dependencies here: pip install openai numpy pandas scikit-learn python-dotenv Why Traditional Testing Breaks Down for LLM Applications If you've written tests for regular software, you know the drill. Function goes in, value comes out, you assert they match. Clean, simple, and done. But LLMs break that entire model. And not in one way, but in several that compound on each other. First, the outputs aren't determinist

could be perfectly good. You can't assertEqual your way through that. And third, nothing breaks visibly and there's no error, crash, or red line in your logs. The model just quietly returns a polished, confident wrong answer. Your uptime dashboard says 100% while your users are getting nonsense. This is the one that really gets you when an LLM fails. So you can't just test LLM apps the way you test a REST API. You need scoring instead of pass/fail. You need to evaluate batches of outputs not individual ones. And you need something that runs continuously because the quality can drift over time without you changing a single line of code. The Three Layers of LLM Evaluation The approach I've lan

The word regression literally means going backwards: your system was handling a question correctly and now after your change, it isn't. correction against push-out bias** [43] + **FE validation for local notch mechanics** [56] [61]. # BOOKKEEPER-AGENT AT — E/A Repository Version: 1.0.0 Scope: österreichisches Einzelunternehmen, Einnahmen-Ausgaben-Rechnung (§ 4 Abs. 3 EStG), Steuerjahr 2025. ## Ziel Deterministischer, auditierbarer Vorbereitungs-Stack für Bank-/Belegdaten, Rule-Pack-Prüfung, Review Queue und Anlagevermögen/AfA. Keine autonome Steuerentscheidung, Buchung oder Einreichung. ## Architektur `SOURCE > RULE > CALCULATION > LLM > HUMAN_GATE` - `rules/AT/2025/`: steuerjahrbezogene, prüfbare Regeln mit amtlichen Quellen. - `schemas/`: kanonische JSON-Schemas. - `src/bookkeeper_at/`: deterministische Python-Logik. - `config/`: Mandanten-/Quellenprofile ohne Geheimnisse. - `tests/`: Golden/Smoke-Tests. - `docs/`: Go

- No credentials, tax IDs or personal secrets in repository files. - Evidence stays in the dedicated evidence root. - Production evidence must not be publicly writable. - Hash originals before normalization; audit events are append-only.

# BOOKKEEPER-AGENT AT — System Prompt v1.0.0 Du bist ein Buchhaltungs- und Rechnungswesen-Assistent für die österreichische Einnahmen-Ausgaben-Rechnung. Arbeite strikt nach `SOURCE > RULE > CALCULATION > LLM` und `PRIMARY > VERIFIED > DERIVED > CONTEXT`. ## Pflichtregeln - Fehlende Werte nie erfinden: `NULL`, `MISSING_EVIDENCE`. - Widerspruch: `CONFLICT -> HUMAN_REVIEW`. - Suchtreffer/Index = Locator, nicht Evidenz. - Originalquelle unverändert lassen; Transformationen mit Source-ID, Hash und Rule-ID dokumentieren. - Geld ausschließlich als Decimal-String. - Steuerjahr, Rule-Pack-Version und Quellenstand in jedem Run fixieren. - Nur schema-validierte und fachlich zugelassene Datensätze aggre

# Deployment Local: `pip install -e '.[dev]' && bookkeeper-at smoke && pytest -q` Docker: `docker build -t bookkeeper-at:1.0.0 .` then `docker run --rm bookkeeper-at:1.0.0 smoke`. Drive is the SSOT/document repository and evidence locator, not the runtime filesystem. Sync/export to a local Git worktree for execution. Keep KB-029 original evidence read-only to automated processing.

# Release Checklist - [x] Syntax/smoke locally validated. - [x] 2025 core Rule-Pack with official RIS references. - [x] AfA/GWG deterministic MVP and tests. - [x] Asset/transaction/review/audit/pipeline schemas. - [ ] Exact official E1a-2025 field mapping independently locked. - [ ] VAT NET/GROSS method confirmed for actual business/year. - [ ] Profession/entity-specific UGB scope confirmed. - [ ] Drive evidence permissions hardened; `anyone:writer` removed. - [ ] Tax adviser/accounting professional releases material tax rules. Until open material gates are closed: `DRAFT_FOR_HUMAN_REVIEW`.

# Architecture 1. **Evidence**: immutable originals and bank exports in KB-029. 2. **Normalization**: deterministic parsers -> canonical JSON. 3. **Rule-Pack**: tax-year-specific rules, official sources, fail-closed. 4. **Calculation**: Decimal, stable IDs, reconciliation, AfA. 5. **LLM**: explanation, candidate classification, review questions only. 6. **Human Gate**: material tax treatment and final release. Indexes, chat, filenames and model memory are never accounting evidence. Every derived value retains `source_ref`, rule identifier and transformation context.

# Anlagevermögen / AfA — MVP Automated: Anlagekartei fields under EStG § 7 Abs. 3, linear AfA under § 7 Abs. 1, full/half-year rule under § 7 Abs. 2 for calendar-year profiles, and explicitly eligible GWG under § 13 up to EUR 1,000. Human review: degressive AfA, buildings, motor vehicles, intangible/special depreciation, mixed private/business use, economic-unit disputes, non-calendar business years, disposals/transfers and extraordinary depreciation. No useful life is inferred by the LLM; it must come from verified policy/source or qualified human review.

# Rule-Pack Governance A rule is deployable only with stable Rule-ID, tax-year/validity, official source, verification status, deterministic behavior or explicit HUMAN_REVIEW, and tests for automated logic. Historical released packs are immutable; legal changes create a new version.
